title: Build a generic stack in Rust — 3 turns
description: Three turns build a generic stack: turn 1 push/pop/peek, turn 2 is_empty/size, turn 3 From<Vec<T>> impl.

task_spec.prompt: Implement `push(&mut self, value: T)`, `pop(&mut self) -> Option<T>`, and `peek(&self) -> Option<&T>` in `src/lib.rs`. Use `self.data.push(value)` for push, `self.data.pop()` for pop, and `self.data.last()` for peek. Run `cargo test --quiet`.
followup_prompts: Good. Now implement `size(&self) -> usize` and `is_empty(&self) -> bool` — both delegate to `self.data`. Run `cargo test --quiet` and fix any failures.
Final step: implement `From<Vec<T>> for Stack<T>` — construct a Stack with `data: v` so the last element of the vec is the top of the stack. Run `cargo test --quiet` — all 4 tests must pass.
success_criteria: peek returns reference to top without removing it
From<Vec<T>> uses vec directly (last element is top)
